answer.sourceLine: This one is genuinely his. Wikiquote’s sourced section for Awaken the Giant Within prints the sentence and cites page 85. The book was first published in 1991 by Summit Books in New York; the page numbering belongs to the 1992 Simon & Schuster edition that Wikiquote cites.

source.excerpt: All personal breakthroughs begin with a change in beliefs. So how do we change? The most effective way is to get your brain to associate massive pain to the old belief.
trail: Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗ for Awaken the Giant Within (1992) prints this sentence and cites page 85. We read the page’s raw wikitext rather than a summary, so the wording and the page number are as Wikiquote states them.

The edition history checks out independently: the Internet Archive catalogue record ↗ gives “New York: Simon & Schuster, 1992,” 552 pages, 1st Fireside edition, and notes that it was “originally published: New York : Summit Books, c1991” — which is why this page dates the work to 1991 and the pagination to 1992.

Limit of what we checked: the page location rests on Wikiquote’s citation. The Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted and Google Books returned a bot challenge, so we did not confirm page 85 against the book’s own text.
source.excerptNote: Wikiquote bolds the first sentence — the part that circulates — and prints the paragraph that follows it, in which Robbins gives his answer: associate pain with the old belief.

author.bio: Tony Robbins, born Anthony J. Mahavoric in 1960, built the modern self-help seminar into an industry. Unlimited Power (1986) made his name and Awaken the Giant Within (1991) became the book most often quoted from, usually one sentence at a time. The lines that circulate from it are typically the opening sentence of a longer paragraph, which is why so many Robbins quotations are genuine but truncated.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: This is a thesis sentence rather than a maxim. It opens the passage where Robbins sets out his method for changing a belief, which is to attach enough pain to the old one that the brain abandons it.
The quotable half travels on its own and sounds like encouragement. The paragraph it opens is considerably more mechanical, and rather more interesting.
detailsBody: Awaken the Giant Within is a 1991 book of about 550 pages, and the lines quoted from it are almost always single sentences lifted from the start of a paragraph. That is worth knowing before trusting any short Robbins quotation: the attribution is usually fine, and the sentence is usually only part of what he wrote.
context.pull: The belief changes first; everything else follows it.
